topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students and outlines the scope and focus of the lecture on inflammation.

topics.label: Innate Immune Recognition and Receptor Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system identifies infections and cellular damage using molecular patterns, receptor families, and downstream signaling pathways.

topics.label: Inflammatory Response, Leukocyte Trafficking, and Systemic Effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how sentinel cells trigger the inflammatory cascade, direct leukocyte recruitment into tissues, drain fluid to lymph nodes, and potentially cause severe systemic pathology.

topics.label: Resolution, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how acute inflammatory reactions are turned off, how damaged tissues are repaired, and how persistent stimuli lead to chronic inflammation or granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the topic for the following lecture.
